Subject: Initial DPA redlines and audit scope — Redwood DPA v2

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our legal team attached a list of DPA redlines and a short questionnaire outlining the audit scope we'd need to support our regulatory requirements. High-level asks below:

- Confirmation of subprocessors and the ability to provide a current list and 30 days notice for additions.
- Data transfer mechanism for EU/UK data (SCCs or equivalent) and an explanation of hosting regions.
- Audit rights: we need the ability to conduct an independent audit (third-party) or Redwood-provided evidence with a 30-day notice window. Scope: SOC 2 Type II, pen test summary, configuration logs for the affected services.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II summary, pen test executive summary, and historic incident reports (high level).

We attached our redlines (Acme_DPA_request_20261115.docx). Please let us know if you can accept the audit wording and provide the attachments above. Also indicate whether you can sign with DocuSign or AdobeSign and the expected timeline.

Sara
Sara Long
Sr. Counsel, Acme Biotech

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Lauren (Security) and Karthik (Privacy/Legal) so we can get everything over to you in one pass.

Quick answers up front:
- Subprocessors: we can provide a current CSV of subprocessors (attached) and will give 30 days notice for material additions.
- Data transfers: we support SCCs for EU/UK transfers and have U.S./EU contractual language in our DPA; we'll include the standard clause set in the redline.
- Audit rights: we want to be pragmatic about scope. We're happy to support third-party audits under an NDA for SOC 2 Type II and a pen test executive summary. For operational logs and live access, we typically offer remote evidence packages and a limited onsite option when mutually agreed with 30 days notice.

I've uploaded an initial redline of the DPA with proposed language that narrows the audit scope to avoid unrestricted access while preserving Acme's ability to obtain independent assurance. Attached: Redwood_DPA_redlines_20261116.pdf, SOC2-type2-summary.pdf, PenTest-Executive-Summary.pdf, Subprocessors-2026Q3.csv.

Proposed mutual action plan:
- Nov 16: Redwood sends redline + evidence packets (done)
- Nov 18: Acme to review and confirm items for negotiation
- Nov 22: Final DPA agreed and DocuSign envelope created
- Nov 29: Signed DPA returned

If that timeline works, we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and include the DPA and a separate subprocessor addendum.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_redlines_20261116.pdf (redline), SOC2-type2-summary.pdf, PenTest-Executive-Summary.pdf, Subprocessors-2026Q3.csv

Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and audit scope — Redwood DPA v2

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the evidence packet. A few items from our side after initial review:

1) Audit rights: Acme requires the ability to engage an independent third-party auditor and, where necessary for high-risk controls, perform an onsite inspection. Can Redwood agree to an onsite option for 1 audit per 12 months, subject to reasonable safety and scheduling constraints?

2) Logs & live access: we accept a remote evidence package for most items, but for a limited subset (control IDs we will flag) we'd want more granular access. Please confirm whether you can provide redacted logs for a 90-day window.

3) Subprocessors: the CSV looks good; please confirm whether any of the subprocessors operate outside the EU/UK and the locations of data at rest.

4) Signing: we prefer DocuSign. If you can send the envelope with your final redlines, we'll route for signature.

If you can confirm onsite audit allowance and the logs window, we'll proceed to mark the non-negotiable items and return a clean copy to sign.

Best,
Sara
